Origination-basis caveat: pre-2020 vintages have incomplete early-life data (loans enter ABS-EE only when their deal begins reporting). Older curves may understate cumulative losses.
Select one or more issuers to view repossession data.
How to read this tab. “Months on book” (MOB) = months since origination. Cumulative default rate at MOB N is the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the probability a loan will have charged off between origination and month N. Loans that paid off or remain active are handled via right-censoring. Commercial / dealer bureau scores excluded; only consumer credit bureau scores 300–900.

Cumulative Default by Score Band

All issuers pooled. Each line = KM cumulative default rate for that Score band.

Default Rate — Issuer × Credit Score

KM cumulative default at a fixed loan age. Cells with <200 loans shown blank.

Modification Rate by Issuer

Cumulative % of loans modified (extended, rate-reduced, etc.) by MOB. Higher = more distressed servicing activity.

Vintage Comparison

For a given Score band, has underwriting / macro shifted the default curve over time?

Issuer Risk Ranking — Raw vs. Score-Adjusted

Raw = actual book default rate. Adjusted = default rate if they had the market’s credit score mix. Δ = book composition effect.
